title: You Tapped Your Card. The Money Didn't Move. | Money Explained #1
simplified: Simplified model: one card network and one merchant bank shown; real flows can add processors; timings vary by bank, card type and country. The amount is an EXAMPLE with no currency.

hook_candidates.text: You just paid. But your money hasn't moved yet.
Watch this clock. Your tap took one second. The money takes a day.
The shop said APPROVED. It still has none of your money.
Where does your money go when you tap? Nowhere, yet.
Your card doesn't carry money. So what did it just send?

parts.text: But your money hasn't moved yet.
The money takes a day or more.
Your tap sends a message, not money,
parts.tts: Your tap sends a message, not money,

parts.text: through the card network to your bank.
Your bank checks you can pay,
So the shop has a yes,
Later, the shop sends its taps in one batch.

sources: Approval in seconds: card authorization 'happens in seconds'; 'with an average network response time of 130 milliseconds' (2012 data). Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Payment Cards Center discussion paper 'Clearing and Settlement of Interbank Card Transactions' (October 2013), https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/frbp/assets/consumer-finance/discussion-papers/D-2013-October-Clearing-Settlement.pdf

Message, not money, via network to the issuing bank: authorization is 'routed through the card network to the issuing bank), with an approval or decline message returned back to the acceptance point'. U.S. Treasury Bureau of the Fiscal Service, How CAS Works (updated 25 Feb 2026), https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/card-acquiring-service-cas/how-cas-works
Hold on the amount: at settlement 'the authorization hold that retains the funds pledged by the cardholder to the merchant is dropped'. Philadelphia Fed (above).

Batch: drafts 'are stored in a batch until the merchant conducts batch processing. This typically occurs at least once a day'; 'merchants submit their authorized transactions to their acquirer in batch mode, not as individual transactions'. Philadelphia Fed (above).

Money moves at settlement: settlement 'is completed when the seller's bank account is credited with, and the buyer's account is debited for' the amount; clearing is 'the nonmonetary exchange of transaction-related information'. Philadelphia Fed (above).

'A day or more': 'most merchants' accounts are automatically credited within 24 hours of entering their drafts into settlement'; 'settlement processing generally occurs Monday through Friday' (US). Philadelphia Fed (above). Treasury CAS: 'next day funds availability' (above). Timing varies by country and bank; stated as 'a day or more', on screen 'USUALLY 1+ DAY'.
Mechanism only; no product, network, bank or card named or recommended.
